q: Which metal is the best conductor?
Which metals would float on water?
Sodium only: its density (0.97) is less than water’s (1.0).
Metal atoms lose outer electrons into a "sea" of delocalised electrons that can move through the structure carrying charge.
Power lines use aluminium, not copper or silver. Use the data to explain.
Aluminium conducts fairly well (61) and has one third the density of copper, so long cables are lighter; silver is far too expensive.
